'''Salomé Minerva Angélica Martínez Salazar''' is a Chilean mathematician and a full professor in the Department of Mathematical Engineering at the [[University of Chile]], where she directs the Mathematics Education Laboratory in the Center for Mathematical Modeling.{{r|pdi|uc}} Her doctoral research was in [[mathematical biology]]; more recently she has focused on [[mathematics education]].{{r|noten}}

==Education and career==
Martínez is the daughter of Chilean mathematician {{ill|Servet Martínez|es}}.{{r|noten}}
She earned a degree in mathematical engineering from the University of Chile in 1995, and completed her Ph.D. in the United States at the [[University of Minnesota]] in 2000.{{r|pdi|uc}} Her doctoral dissertation, ''The Effects of Diffusion and Cross-Diffusion for the 3 × 3 Lotka-Volterra Competition System'', was supervised by [[Wei-Ming Ni]].{{r|mg}}

After postdoctoral research at [[Georgia Tech]] from 2000 to 2002, she returned to the University of Chile as an associate professor in 2002. She has been a full professor there since 2017,{{r|pdi}} becoming the first female professor in the Department of Mathematical Engineering.{{r|noten}} She was the university's Director of Gender and Diversity from 2018 to 2019.{{r|pdi}}

==Recognition==
Martínez was a member of the [[Global Young Academy]] from 2010 to 2012.{{r|gya}} She became a corresponding member of the Chilean Academy of Sciences in 2018.{{r|pdi}}

In 1996, the Institute of Engineers of Chile gave Martínez the Marcos Orrego Puelma Prize, naming her as the best engineering graduate of the year in Chile.{{r|pdi}} The Chilean Academy of Sciences gave Martínez their inaugural Adelina Gutierrez Award for the Academic Excellence of Young Female Scientists in 2012.{{r|pdi|noten}} She was a 2018 recipient of the UNESCO–Hamdan Prize for Teacher Development of [[UNESCO]] and the Hamdan Bin Rashid Al Maktoum foundation. [[Andrés Bello National University]] gave her its Prize for Merit in Education in 2021.{{r|pdi}}
